title: The Hindu Morning Digest : November 18 , 2026
full_text: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post. Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses storyline 1 World needs peace, stability, predictability: Modi in Manila Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) called for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world as he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit, and the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila, Philippines. He made a number of proposals aimed at maritime security, protecting critical minerals supply chains, and enhancing trade. The Quad Summit, which was being held for the first time in a non-member country, was hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump and was also attended by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, apart from Mr. Modi. The leaders issued a joint statement opposing economic and maritime “coercion” in the Indo-Pacific, and Mr. Modi announced that India would host the first Quad Business Forum in Mumbai in 2027. World needs peace, stability, predictability: Modi in Manila storyline 1 Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time. “India is a nation of extraordinary innovation and ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William. Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change storyline 1 Congress-SP talks on U.P. seat-sharing deferred after Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh meet A meeting that had been scheduled for Tuesday (November 17, 2026) for the Congress and the Samajwadi Party (SP) to discuss seat-sharing in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections has been deferred following talks between the top leadership of the two parties. No fresh date has been set for the meeting, with sources saying that it is expected to take place “in a few days”. Sources indicated that the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and SP president Akhilesh Yadav had a word on the sidelines of the launch event of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, held in Delhi on Monday (November 16). Congress-SP talks on U.P. seat-sharing deferred after Rahul, Akhilesh meet storyline 1 Nearly 75 lakh names added to draft SSR voter lists in 13 States and UTs Months after final voter lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process (SSR). The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list. This means there has been a cumulative increase of 1.64 %. Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs storyline 1 Thirupparankundram row: T.N. government pushes for stay of High Court order to avoid breach of peace The Tamil Nadu government urged the Supreme Court on Tuesday to stay a Madras High Court decision of January 2026 which confirmed its earlier order to the Arulmigu Subramaniswamy Temple devasthanam or management body to light the Karthigai Deepam on a stone pillar located atop the Thirupparankundram Hill. The Division Bench of the High Court in January had upheld the earlier Single Judge order, while brushing aside fears expressed by the State that such an action would be a sure recipe for “disturbance of public tranquility and peace”, given the fact that the stone pillar was proximate to a dargah. The High Court had dismissed the fears as an “imaginary ghost”. Thirupparankundram row: T.N. govt pushes for stay of HC order to avoid breach of peace storyline 1 Opposition, OBC group voice concerns on 287 ‘other’ religions in the Census Opposition leaders and the All India Other Backward Classes Students’ Association on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) raised questions about the way in which the 2027 Census is being conducted, reacting to The Hindu’s report on the self-enumeration portal listing as many as 287 options in a drop-down box for “Other” religions, including ‘ISKCON’, ‘Ramkrishna Paramhansa’, Shia, Sunni, and ‘Pentacostal’. This list vanished from the portal within hours of The Hindu’s queries about it, posed to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.   Opposition, OBC group voice concerns on 287 ‘other’ religions in the Census storyline 1 India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home. “Neither India nor any other country can dictate terms on this,” Mr. Zahed said during a media briefing when asked for comments on a media report saying New Delhi had hinted at two conditions for handing over Hasina. India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser storyline 1 U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S. A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner. U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S. storyline 1 Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry A Russian military transport plane crashed in western Siberia on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), killing all 19 people on board, the Defence Ministry said. Preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure. The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash. The An-12 typically has a crew of six. Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry storyline 1 Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid Bangladesh’s first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country’s northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials. The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources. Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid storyline 1 Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
